bull.b: Arm’s exceptionally high gross margins and robust trailing‑12‑month free cash flow stem from an IP licensing and royalty model that scales with chip shipments. This durable margin profile supports sustained R&D investment, funds strategic initiatives, and preserves financial flexibility over multiple years.

bull.t: Licensing + Royalty Business and Ecosystem Scale
bull.b: A dual revenue model (upfront licenses plus usage royalties) tied to a large developer ecosystem creates persistent customer lock‑in and multi‑cycle revenue streams. Broad software/tooling adoption and developer scale lower switching costs and raise barriers for competitors long term.

bull.t: Data Center Momentum & AGI CPU Opportunity
bull.b: Rapid data‑center royalty growth and a growing AGI CPU pipeline represent a structural expansion into AI infrastructure. If sustained, this diversifies revenue beyond mobile, increases high‑value license and royalty pools, and creates a multi‑year growth runway tied to secular AI compute demand.

bear.b: Arm still depends materially on handset volumes for royalty flow; elevated memory costs raised BOMs and reduced handset demand, directly moderating royalties. This exposure to end‑market cycles can tighten near‑term revenue visibility and slow royalty growth across multiple quarters.

bear.t: Supply‑Chain Constraints for AGI CPU Ramp
bear.b: Scaling Arm’s AGI CPU depends on external manufacturing capacity. Persistent wafer, substrate, test and memory bottlenecks can delay shipments, cap near‑term royalties/licenses and defer margin improvement, pushing meaningful upside out toward FY29–FY30 and raising execution risk.

bear.t: Initial AGI CPU Margins and Elevated OpEx
bear.b: First‑generation AGI CPUs will start with substantially lower gross margins than Arm’s core IP business and require a multi‑year path to ~50%. Combined with rising R&D and operating expense, this delays accretive margin and free‑cash‐flow benefits and raises near‑term profitability variability.
